description:
Put the same independent questions to each of many items — a queue of tickets, a page of comments, rows of records — and get typed answers per item.

How it runs: each item is its own request to Jev, carrying its state and every question, so an item costs what a `jev_ask` call with those questions costs. Requests go out a few at a time and are paced to the key's rate limit. Use `jev_ask` for a single item.

How to design the call:
- `items` holds 1 to 100 records, each with its own `state`. Give every item an `id` — the record's own id, such as a ticket number — so its results map back without counting positions; without ids, items are labelled by position from "0".
- `questions` follows the same rules as in `jev_ask`, and every item is judged against all of them, independently.

Reading the result: `counts` gives the totals. `answers[item id][question id]` holds an answered item's answers, shaped as in `jev_ask`; `confidence` says how concentrated a distribution is, not how likely the answer is to be correct. `errors[item id]` holds an item that failed, with its `code` and whether it is `retryable`. When the call ends early — a rejected key, a rate limit it cannot wait out, several failures in a row, or its time budget — `stopped` says why and `not_sent` lists the items never sent. Send those, and any retryable errors, in a later call, after `retry_after_ms` when it is given.

items.description: The records to judge, 1 to 100 per call. Each is sent as its own request, with every question.

id.description: Your label for this item, used as its key in `answers` or `errors`. Use the record's own id, such as a ticket number, so results map back without counting positions. Give every item an id or none; without ids, items are labelled by position from "0". Never sent to the model.

state.description: This item's content, judged on its own: text, an object of named fields, or an array of records. Fetch external records first — a URL here is not a request to browse.

model.description: Model alias. Omit to use the server default (`openjev`).

criteria.description: The possible answers. For choice, an object of option name to description (or an array of option names as shorthand); up to 255 options. For score, an ordered array of levels, lowest first; up to 10. For noul, optional {"true": ..., "false": ...} descriptions.

instructions.description: The judgment to make, written out in full. A clear specific string is usually enough; use an object or array when the judgment, its scope, and its constraints belong together. The question id is not sent to the model, so never rely on it to carry meaning.

type.description: choice: one of a set of named options. score: a position on an ordered scale. noul: a yes/no probability.

questions.description: Question id to question definition, as in `jev_ask`. Non-empty. Every item is asked every question.

name: jev_batch

answers.description: Item id to that item's answers, keyed by question id as in `jev_ask`.

counts.description: How many items were answered, failed, or never sent.

errors.description: Item id to the failure of an item that was sent but not answered.

hints.description: Non-blocking advice about this request, when there is any.

not_sent.description: Ids of the items never sent because the call stopped early.

stopped.description: Present when the call ended before sending every item: why, and whether the unsent items can be sent again as they are.

usage.description: Tokens summed over the answered items.

title: Jev batch (many items)
